contentHtml:
Hyderabad: NATCO Pharma Limited has announced an additional investment of USD 14 million in US-based biotechnology company eGenesis, Inc., taking its total investment in the clinical-stage company to USD 22 million.

NATCO Pharma said the latest investment will be made through its wholly owned subsidiaries, NATCO Pharma (Canada) Inc. and NATCO Pharma South Africa Proprietary Limited.

The Canadian subsidiary will invest USD 9.50 million, while the South African subsidiary will contribute USD 4.50 million through convertible promissory notes.

The notes carry an interest rate of 8% compounded annually. NATCO Pharma clarified that no additional shares in eGenesis are being acquired at the time of completion of the transaction. The investment is expected to be completed by September 30, 2026.

The latest investment builds on NATCO Pharma's previous USD 8 million investment in eGenesis through preferred stock in 2024, bringing the pharmaceutical company's cumulative investment in eGenesis to USD 22 million.

According to NATCO Pharma, the investment is aimed at supporting "new-age therapeutic programmes addressing critical unmet medical needs."

eGenesis focuses on gene-engineered organs for transplantation.

eGenesis Develops Gene-Engineered Organs

Cambridge, Massachusetts-based eGenesis is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing genetically engineered porcine organs for transplantation into humans.

The company uses a multiplex gene-editing and genome-engineering platform designed to address molecular incompatibilities, viral risks and mechanisms of human rejection associated with cross-species transplantation.

Its eGenesis Genome Engineering and Production (EGEN™) Platform is being used to advance programs in kidney transplantation, acute liver failure and heart transplantation.

The company is currently conducting clinical trials involving porcine kidney transplantation in humans and porcine liver perfusion, with the broader goal of addressing the shortage of human donor organs for patients with acute and chronic organ failure.

In March 2024, eGenesis announced what it described as the world's first porcine kidney transplant in a living patient. The procedure was authorized by the US Food and Drug Administration under its Expanded Access pathway.

According to NATCO Pharma, porcine kidney transplants were subsequently performed in two additional patients.

Founded on October 1, 2015, eGenesis is currently a pre-revenue clinical-stage company with operations in the United States.

Hyderabad-headquartered NATCO Pharma develops, manufactures and distributes generic and branded pharmaceuticals, specialty pharmaceuticals, active pharmaceutical ingredients and crop protection products.

The company has a focus on oncology and limited-competition molecules in the US market, with its manufacturing facilities supplying more than 50 global markets.
